rows.requirement: **ID-01** Every object listed in §2.1 has an `id` that is unique within the project across all types, assigned at   creation and never changed or reused for the lifetime of the project, including after deletion.
rows.note: fixed; all split entry maps, cross-type/global/local duplicate controls pass; allocation transactions still C1.2
rows.r1_note: C11-R1-01; allocation/immutability also depend on C1.2.

rows.requirement: **ID-02** IDs are opaque strings of at most 64 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. **Design decision:** a short type   prefix, an underscore and a 26-character time-ordered random identifier (ULID-style, 128 bits), e.g.   `sw_01JA8Q6V8Z3K7M2N5P4R9S0T1W`. With 128 random bits IDs are also unique across projects, which colour identity and   library links rely on.
rows.note: fixed; 800000 IDs each for system and seeded shared generators, no collisions
rows.r1_note: 1,000,000 sequential IDs pass; cloning the system generator duplicates IDs (C11-R1-20). Opaque input IDs intentionally allow lowercase/non-ULID forms.

rows.requirement: **ID-03** Objects inside a drawing (`drawingNode`, `stroke`) and keys inside a channel MAY carry short IDs unique only   within their container (e.g. `s42`). Their project-wide form is `<containerId>/<localId>` (e.g. `dr_01JA…/s42`);   every interface that accepts an `id` accepts the compound form. Zones are derived and have **transient** IDs that are   valid only for the drawing revision at which they were read (section 02 §3.12).
rows.note: Scoped nodes/strokes/keys and compound refs; motionPoint added per SI-006.

rows.requirement: **ID-04** IDs survive save and load, undo and redo (undoing a deletion restores the original ID), and moves within   the project (re-parenting, re-ordering, moving a drawing between cells).
rows.note: C1.2 undo/redo/moves, C1.3 save/load (handoff gaps 1,5).

rows.requirement: **ID-05** Copy/paste, duplicate, template insertion and `doc.import.json` with `idPolicy: "new"` assign **new** IDs to   every created object and rewrite internal references consistently — **except colour IDs**:   - pasted or inserted artwork keeps the colour IDs it uses; when the target project lacks a colour ID it is recovered     from the drawing's colour-recovery data (§4.11; rules in section 03);   - duplicating a palette style keeps colour IDs (a style is another value set for the same swatches); duplicating a     palette creates new colour IDs (section 03);   - importing a `.animpal` keeps palette, style and colour IDs, with the conflict policy of section 03.
rows.note: C1.2 edit commands and C1.3 import (gaps 1,5).

rows.requirement: **ID-06** Library, folder and item IDs are globally unique and stable across renames and moves (section 08 LIB-002);   linked usages refer to `libraryId` + `itemId`.
rows.note: Generator/type representation present; rename/move/library copy policy belongs to commands C1.2/C9.1.

rows.requirement: **ID-07** "No colour" is `null`; there are no reserved ID values.
rows.note: Option<Id>, no reserved colour IDs.

rows.requirement: **REV-01** The document has a monotonically increasing integer **`documentRev`**. Every committed transaction (one   command, one atomic `batch`, one undo or redo step, one load-time repair set) increments it by exactly 1. Queries never   change it.
rows.note: documentRev and <= integrity present; commit stamping C1.2 gap 1.

rows.requirement: **REV-02** Each object's `rev` is the `documentRev` of the last transaction that changed one of its own persisted   properties or the membership or order of its own child collections. A change to a child's properties does not change   the parent's `rev`. Content edits of a drawing (strokes, nodes) change the drawing's `rev` as well as the affected   node's (section 02 §3.12 calls this the drawing revision).
rows.note: Own-view mechanism present; C11-R1-03/04; stamping C1.2 gap 1.

rows.requirement: **REV-03** Undo and redo are new transactions: they increment `documentRev` and stamp the affected objects with the   new value. Revisions never decrease.
rows.note: C1.2 undo/redo stamping, gap 1.

rows.requirement: **REV-04** `documentRev` and every object's `rev` are persisted, so `doc.diff` and `expectRev` work across save and   reopen. The project's clean marker (01 §3.5) is the undo position at the last save; `savedRev` (the `documentRev`   written by the last save) is reported by `doc.state.get`.
rows.note: Fields and integrity present; persisted manifest/C1.3 and expectRev/C1.2.

rows.requirement: **REV-05** Every mutating command that targets existing objects accepts `expectRev` (an int for a single target, or a   map `{id: rev}`; 11 §7.2). If any listed object's current `rev` differs, the command fails with `rev.conflict`   (`details.currentRev`, and the object's current JSON when it is smaller than 64 KiB) and changes nothing.
rows.note: C1.2 expectRev, gap 1.

rows.requirement: **REV-06** GUI and agent edits share one serialised transaction queue. A GUI gesture in progress (e.g. a stroke being   drawn) is committed as one transaction when it ends; agent commands arriving meanwhile wait or fail with `ui.busy`   as defined in 11 §6.4.
rows.note: C1.2 transaction queue, gap 1.

rows.requirement: **FMT-01** Opening a path that is a file reads the package form; opening a path that is a directory reads the folder   form. Both forms MUST load to the identical document, and saving either form produces entries with identical bytes   for the same document (except zip framing).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **FMT-02** A project remembers its form; Save writes the same form. Converting between forms is a save-as-copy in the   other form (`doc.package.export`) followed by opening the copy, or Save As (01) with a folder destination   (see design decisions).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **FMT-03** When a folder-form project is created, the application writes a `.gitignore` (only if none exists) listing   `cache/`, `session.json` and `*.lock`, and a `.gitattributes` marking `*.png`, `media/**` and `textures/**` as binary.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **ZIP-01** Standard zip (PKWARE APPNOTE) with ZIP64 support. Entry names are UTF-8 (language-encoding flag set), use   `/` separators, are relative, contain no `..` segment, no drive letters and no leading `/`. A package violating this is   rejected (`project.invalidFormat`, detail `unsafeEntry`) without extracting anything.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **ZIP-02** The first entry is `mimetype`, stored uncompressed, without extra fields, containing exactly the media type   string (no newline), so the type can be identified from the first bytes of the file.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **ZIP-03** JSON entries are deflate-compressed. Already-compressed media (PNG, MP3, AAC, MP4, MOV) SHOULD be stored.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **ZIP-04** Readers MUST ignore unknown entries outside the reserved names of §6.3 and MUST preserve them on save   (copy unchanged), so that other tools can add data.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **ZIP-05** No encryption, no signatures. Integrity is provided by the SHA-256 list in the manifest (§6.4).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **ZIP-06** Readers MUST NOT trust declared sizes: decompression is bounded by the manifest sizes plus a margin and by a   global limit (protection against zip bombs); exceeding them aborts the load (`project.invalidFormat`, `sizeLimit`).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **LAY-01** Every object lives in exactly one entry. Entries split the model at: project, palette, scene, element,   drawing bank and drawing. All other objects are inline in their parent's entry.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **LAY-02** Entry names use object IDs, never display names, so renames do not move files. Texture file names are   generated unique names (e.g. `<swatchName>-<styleName>.png` made unique) and stay stable once written.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **LAY-03** Entries of deleted objects disappear on the next save; until then the deletion is undoable.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **LAY-04** A clean (unmodified) project saves without rewriting any entry. In folder form, only entries whose bytes   changed are rewritten.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **JSON-01** UTF-8 without BOM, `\n` line endings, two-space indentation, final newline.
rows.note: UTF-8, LF, two spaces, newline; golden/property controls pass.

rows.requirement: **JSON-02** Object keys in schema order: envelope (`id`/`colourId`, `type`, `rev`, `name`) first, then the type's   properties in the order of its schema, then `meta`, then `ext`; unknown keys (from newer minor versions) last in   lexicographic order.
rows.note: fixed; schema order and recursively sorted map keys; SI-014 correctly notes unspecified map order
rows.r1_note: C11-R1-06; structs ordered, free-form maps/scene.paletteStyles not canonical.

rows.requirement: **JSON-03** Numbers in the shortest form that round-trips to the same double; `-0` written as `0`; integers without   a fraction. Arrays of small numeric tuples (stroke points, exposure runs, pressure samples) are written on one line   per tuple.
rows.note: fixed; finite canonical numbers; exact large integer transport separately verified
rows.r1_note: Finite vectors/tuples/-0 pass; generic serialization admits nonfinite -> null, C11-R1-16.

rows.requirement: **JSON-04** Default-valued optional properties MAY be omitted only where the schema marks them `x-omitDefault`   (`meta`, `ext`, notes, empty maps); everything else is written explicitly.
rows.note: x-omitDefault rules match serializer omissions.

rows.requirement: **JSON-05** Saving the same document twice produces byte-identical entries.
rows.note: fixed for validated model objects; input depth100 protects writer128; generic wire mismatch is row412
rows.r1_note: Same constructed document stable; not all accepted objects serializable, C11-R1-09, or equal documents identical, C11-R1-06.

rows.requirement: **VER-01** The format version is `MAJOR.MINOR`. A **minor** increment only adds optional properties, types or enum   values that older readers may ignore; a **major** increment is any other change.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **VER-02** On open: if `minReaderVersion` is newer than the reader, or the major version is newer, or a   `requiredFeatures` entry is unknown, the open fails with `project.unsupportedVersion` (01 §3.2), naming the versions   or features. If only the minor version is newer, the project opens with warning `project.newerMinorVersion`; unknown   properties, types and enum values are preserved verbatim (as opaque JSON) and written back unchanged on save; objects   with unknown enum values are read-only (`doc.unknownValue` on edit attempts).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **VER-03** Older versions are **migrated in memory** on open by a chain of migration steps (N → N+1), each a pure   function from the old JSON to the new JSON. Migration never deletes information: anything without a new home is kept   under `ext["app.migrated"]`. Migration does not mark the project modified. The original file is not touched until   the user saves; the first save of a migrated project requires confirmation of the upgrade (`project.formatUpgrade`,   01 §3.2, parameter `allowFormatUpgrade` of `project.save`). The load report records `migratedFrom`.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **VER-04** Every migration step has fixture tests (old file → expected new JSON) that MUST pass before release.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **VER-05** Libraries (§6.11), templates (§6.9) and palette files carry their own `formatVersion` and follow the same   rules (08 §11 for the library upgrade confirmation).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **MED-01 Embedded** assets (default for imported sound and images) are copied byte-for-byte into `media/<assetId>.<ext>`   (`ext` from the source file, lower case). Identical content (same SHA-256) is stored once and shared (07 §2.3).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **MED-02 Linked** assets (media-element sources, 04 §2.5, 07 §1.1) are not copied. The link stores a path relative to   the folder containing the project and the absolute path at link time, or a library item reference. Resolution order   on load: (1) relative path, (2) absolute path, (3) a file with the same name and size in the project's folder,   (4) folders added by the user or agent via `doc.asset.relink {searchFolder}`. Library links resolve through the   library ID and item ID; a newer `versionId` marks the usage for refresh (08 §7.2).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **MED-03** Missing assets never prevent opening: affected objects keep their timing and show placeholders; one   summary warning per open (`project.mediaMissing`, 01 §3.2) lists all missing items; `doc.asset.list {status:"missing"}`   and `doc.validate` report them.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **MED-04** Embedded assets no longer referenced by any object of the project (or its local library) are removed from   the package on save (07 §2.3); while the project is open they stay in memory so undo can restore references.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **MED-05** Bitmap node pixels are stored as PNG entries next to their drawing (§6.3), not as assets.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **MED-06** Waveform peak caches and thumbnails go under `cache/`; a reader MUST work without them and regenerate them   in the background.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **LOAD-01** Drawings MAY be loaded lazily (content parsed on first access) provided every query and command behaves   exactly as if they were loaded; `doc.validate` and `doc.object.find` with content predicates force loading.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **LOAD-02** Cancelling the job leaves no project open (01 §3.2).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **LOAD-03** Loading MUST be deterministic: the same files produce the same document, the same IDs, revisions and   repairs.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **REP-01** Repairs form one transaction with origin `load`, undoable as "Repair on Open"; the project is then   modified (so the user can save the repaired version or discard it).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **REP-02** No repair may silently lose user content: anything removed is listed in the load report with its old JSON.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **SAVE-01 Package form.** Write the complete new package to a temporary file in the destination folder   (`.<name>.animpkg.<random>.tmp`), flush it to stable storage, re-open it and verify the manifest hashes, then   replace the destination atomically (rename-over on POSIX; replace-file with write-through on Windows). Unchanged   entries MAY be copied from the old package without recompression. On any failure the temporary file is deleted and   the destination is untouched (01 §3.6).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **SAVE-02 Folder form.** Write each changed entry to a temporary sibling file, flush, then rename over the target;   write a journal `.save-journal.json` (list of pending renames and deletions) before the first rename and delete it   after the last. `manifest.json` is written last. On open, a leftover journal means an interrupted save: the   application completes the listed renames if every temporary file is present and valid, otherwise rolls back by   deleting the temporaries, and reports `project.saveInterrupted` (warning).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **SAVE-03** Saving is not cancellable once writing has started (01 §3.6); progress is reported per phase   (serialise, write media, write drawings, verify, replace).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **SAVE-04** A save serialises a consistent snapshot taken between transactions; editing MAY continue while the   snapshot is written, and the clean marker is set to the snapshot's undo position.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **SAVE-05** Failures are reported with the codes of 01 §3.6 (`project.saveFailed`, `project.permissionDenied`,   `project.readOnly`) plus `details.reason` ∈ `diskFull`, `fileInUse`, `verifyFailed`, `ioError`.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **BAK-01** After a successful save that replaces an existing version, the previous version is moved (not copied, where   the file system allows) into the per-user backups folder: `<backups>/<projectId>/<savedAt>.animpkg`, plus   `backup.json` listing `{backupId, originalPath, projectName, savedAt, documentRev, sizeBytes}` (01 §3.7).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **BAK-02** Folder-form projects are backed up as a package-form snapshot of the previous version.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **BAK-03** `files.backups.count` versions are kept per project (default 3, 0 = off), oldest removed first.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **BAK-04** Opening a backup (`project.backup.open`) loads it as an untitled copy; the backup itself is never modified.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **AUTO-01** Every `files.autosave.intervalMinutes` (default 5) while the project is modified, a recovery copy is   written to `<recovery>/<recoveryId>/` in **folder form** (so only changed entries are rewritten), together with   `recovery.json` `{recoveryId, projectId, projectName, originalPath, savedAt, documentRev, appVersion, processId}`.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **AUTO-02** Autosave MUST NOT write to the user's project, change the clean marker, the undo history or the project   location (01 §3.7). It serialises a snapshot between transactions on the main thread (copy-on-write; budget ≤ 50 ms   for typical projects) and writes it on a background thread; it is postponed during gestures and modal operations.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **AUTO-03** Untitled (never saved) projects are autosaved too (`originalPath: null`).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **AUTO-04** The recovery folder is deleted after a successful save, a discard-close or a clean quit (01 §3.7).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **REC-01** At launch, recovery folders whose `processId` is not a running instance of the application are offered   (01 §1.1, `project.recovery.list`). Recovery data is validated like a project (§7) before being offered; unusable   data is listed with a reason.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **REC-02** Recovering opens the copy as a **modified** project whose location is `originalPath`, so Save writes to the   original location (01 §3.7). If the original file was saved after the recovery copy (its `savedAt` is newer), the   user is warned before saving over it (`project.recoveryOlderThanFile`).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **RO-01** A project on a read-only location opens read-only (01 §3.2).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **RO-02** While a project is open the application watches its file (or folder). If it is modified by another process,   the user is warned (`project.changedOnDisk`) and offered *reload* (discarding in-memory changes) or *keep mine* (the   next save overwrites, after confirmation). Agents receive the same choice as a `needs_confirmation` result on the   next save.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **LOCK-01** Opening a project for writing creates a lock file next to it (`<package path>.lock`, or `.lock` inside a   folder-form project) containing `{user, host, processId, appVersion, openedAt, heartbeatAt}`; the heartbeat is   refreshed every 60 s and the lock is removed on close.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **LOCK-02** If a live lock held by someone else exists, the project opens read-only and the lock holder is reported   (`project.lockedByOther`, warning; 01 §3.2). A lock whose heartbeat is older than 5 minutes, or whose process is   known dead on the same host, is stale and is taken over with a warning.
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **LOCK-03** Libraries use the same mechanism for write access (08 LIB-006).
rows.note: C1.3 persistence/load/save/versions; C1.4 protocol where applicable; handoff gaps 1,5.

rows.requirement: **AG-01 One model, one schema.** The generic MCP tools of section 11 are thin wrappers over the `doc` commands and   return identical data: `get_object` ≡ `doc.object.get`, `find_objects` / `query` ≡ `doc.object.find`,   `set_properties` ≡ `doc.object.patch` (with `props`), `doc_diff` ≡ `doc.diff`. Their results are object-model JSON   (§2.2, DM-1). Area read models (e.g. `element.get`, `colour.palette.get`, `xsheet.exposures.get`) MUST be projections   of the same data with the same field names, except where a section documents a renamed field (04 reports   `elementType` as `type`).
rows.note: Shared types/schemas present; C1.2 registry, C1.3 doc commands, C1.4 MCP. C11-R1-08/11/12/13.

rows.requirement: **AG-02 Generic patch.** `doc.object.patch` changes any writable persisted property of any object:   - it accepts a JSON merge patch (`props`, RFC 7386 semantics) applied to every target, and/or JSON-Patch operations     (`ops`, RFC 6902: `add`, `remove`, `replace`, `move`, `copy`, `test`) with JSON Pointers into the object;   - the result is validated against the type's schema **and** the semantic rules of the owning section (ranges, name     uniqueness, reference types, locks: `element.locked`, `drawing.locked`) before anything changes;   - a property annotated with `x-command` is applied with exactly the semantics and side effects of that command     (patching an element's `name` ≡ `element.rename`; patching a camera's `camera.fov` ≡ `anim.camera.set`);   - creating, deleting, re-parenting or re-ordering objects and editing child collections is refused with     `doc.structuralChange` naming the area command to use; read-only, derived and transient properties are refused with     `doc.readOnlyProperty`;   - value-typed collections (gradient stops, envelopes, exposure runs, `meta`, `ext`, mapping tables) are patchable;     exposure runs are normalised (§4.7) after the patch;   - all targets change atomically in **one undo step** labelled `label` or "Set <property>"; `dryRun` returns the change     set without applying it; `expectRev` gives optimistic concurrency (REV-05).
rows.note: C1.2 command/executor, gap 1; current inversion blockers C11-R1-03/04.

rows.requirement: **AG-03 Addressing.** All `ref` parameters accept IDs, compound IDs and paths (§2.4) and the special references of 11.   Results always include `id` and the canonical `path`.
